title: Playing dance jobs and USO shows on the side; avoiding the Navy
summary: Most famous drafted musicians went to Great Lakes Navy, which he abhorred; in Kentucky small bands played $5 USO and club dates in nearby towns with an army truck.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Did you get any opportunity to play anything else?
Yes. Now, on the side, all through my Army career, we had different little dance bands, trios,
quartets, whatever we could get together to play jazz, dance music.
Any other musicians you were with whom we might know of?
Well, no, not in the -- most of the well known musicians who were drafted into the armed services were sent to Great Lakes.
The Navy, which I abhored. I was so glad they didn't send me. I thought about all that, and I said now if they send me to Great Lakes and those Navy boys, I don't know what I'd have done, you know.
Was it just the uniform you didn't like, or --

That's right. I couldn't see myself walking with a little round white hat on and a cape hanging on my back, and this ribbon in front. To me that was a -- and I don't know, and it's the wrong image, because a sailor is always supposed to be the toughest human being ever invented, you know, down through history. Yeah.

So anyway, we did have little bands, like for instance when we were in Kentucky we -- of course in that area they had USO, you know, and the churches, and the ordinary people in town, like Evansville, Indiana was a short way from Breckenridge, and they'd hire us to play club date dances, just

like we were in civilian life. And for the USO shows we were paid $5.00, $5.00 a job, and we loved it because it was, you know, we could do what we wanted to do. We'd get away from it, you know. And I remember we had so much work that way, we used to work four or five nights a week. We were killing ourselves, and we'd get back. See, we were allowed to do this by the Colonel. And we'd just call up the office and say we need a truck, we're going to go to so-and-so, Henderson, Kentucky, or you know, whatever the town is. We're going 50 miles, 20 miles. And we'd go to the pool and get the truck and the driver and get in the truck and be driven to the job and he'd wait for us and drive us back to camp.
You had a very good deal there.
